# Quality Contract for Line Counter (Node.js)

Project: `peerfoil-fixture-node` · Assurance: Guided · Revision: 1 · Status: accepted

- **Author:** architect (claude-code, anthropic-claude, session null)
- **Written at:** 2026-10-21T08:45:00Z
- **Pack:** software 0.1.0
- **Architecture revision:** 1

This contract lists the evidence the project needs before work is accepted. Required
evidence blocks completion when it is missing or failed. Recommended evidence is run when
practical and its absence is recorded. Not-applicable evidence names the reason it does
not apply. A model's statement that a check passed is a claim, not evidence.

## Required evidence

| Name | Kind | Procedure |
|---|---|---|
| unit-tests | executable | `["npm", "test"]` in the project root |
| user-journey | human | A person runs `node linecount.js` on a small text file, checks the count against the file in an editor, and records the steps and the result |
| license-check | inspection | Confirm the project still has no dependencies and no copied third-party material |

## Recommended evidence

| Name | Kind | Procedure |
|---|---|---|
| lint | executable | `["node", "--check", "linecount.js"]` then `["node", "--check", "linecount.test.js"]` in the project root |
| failure-handling-check | inspection | Run the command with a missing file and with no argument; expect a readable error on standard error and exit code 1, never a stack trace |
| privacy-check | inspection | Confirm the tool reads only the named file or standard input, prints only a count or an error, and logs nothing |
| accessibility-check | inspection | Confirm terminal output and errors are plain sentences, carry no color-only cues, and the README reads plainly |
| maintainability-review | inspection | Confirm names are descriptive, functions are small, and comments match the code |
| documentation-check | inspection | Confirm the usage line and the README match the shipped behavior, including the --json flag once it lands |

## Not applicable

| Name | Reason |
|---|---|
| build | Node.js runs the source directly; there is no build step |
| dependency-audit | The project declares no dependencies, so there is nothing for a dependency scanner to audit |
| security-scan | The project has no dependencies and no scanner of its own; the security-privacy review lens covers the single source file |
| release-check | The tool is one file run in place; the user-journey evidence already covers running it from a clean checkout |

## Review lenses

| Lens | Focus |
|---|---|
| correctness-reliability | Behavior matches the accepted decisions and plan; failure handling, recovery, and edge cases are covered by evidence |
| security-privacy | Input validation, command and query construction, permissions, credentials, personal data, and dependency risks |
| accessibility-ux | Keyboard use, labels, contrast, error messages, and plain-language output for user-facing surfaces |
| maintainability-docs-licensing-release | Readable code, current documentation, headers and notices, license compatibility, and packaging |

## Completion requirements

1. Every required evidence item for the phase has a current record tied to the exact revision reviewed.
2. Both phase reviewers approved, or the user accepted a recorded reduced-assurance decision.
3. The plan revision reflects every accepted change, TODO, deviation, skipped check, and deferral.
4. The first phase installs, starts, and completes one real user action.
